author: jessica
source: his 2026-10-29 21:34 "Mining contract. Deliver X ore to a POI. Trick is we limit the planets to the ones with that resource", then "yeah draft that"
_note: THE MINING CONTRACT. A crew at a quiet site has run out of an ore; the player brings ten units and drops them in
their hopper. Mined with his own cutter or bought from a vendor, both count: a contractor being a contractor.
THE TRICK IS THE DRAW: only planets that carry the ore, so the job is true where it lands and the ore is local.
It only earns its keep on a MID-RARITY ore. Iron or aluminium are everywhere and sold everywhere, so the filter
would do nothing. Tungsten first; letters b and c swap the ore and the reason, same shape.
A COMMON, NOT A SPECIAL (41a's register): one plain line of stake, no twist. The crew are builders, not miners,
which is the one human note and the answer to 'why not dig it yourselves'.
(1) place.resource: a draw condition on the planet's resources. Same family as 33a's place.planet, keyed on what
the planet carries instead of its name. Whether the engine has a condition for it is the first question.
(2) beats[0].bring: a deliver that takes N of a resource the PLAYER brings, not an item the mission gave him.
His MB11 to MB13 finish on an item put into a container at the site: the prior art for the handover.
Not narrow, so roles only aloud. The ore's name is an item, not a place or faction, so the voice may say it. Pay: med, placeholder.

broadcast: We're builders, not miners, and we've run out of tungsten. There's plenty in the ground if you've got a cutter, and I won't ask if you bought it instead. Ten units in the hopper and we're back to work.
_speech: A foreman with a small, practical stake and no patience for digging. 41a's voice as a stand-in; his ear decides.
